title: Home & everyday objects
goal: Name rooms and household objects, say where things are, and say what there is (and isn't) in a place.
intro:
English uses prepositions *before* a noun (in the room); Telugu uses **case suffixes and postpositions after** it: *గదిలో* (gadilō, room-in), *బల్ల మీద* (balla mīda, table on).

Some nouns change shape before these endings. The most important is *ఇల్లు* (house), which becomes *ఇంటి-*: *ఇంట్లో* (at home), *ఇంటి దగ్గర* (near the house).

vocab.note: Oblique ఇంటి-; at home ఇంట్లో; pl. ఇళ్ళు
Lit. 'lock ear'; colloquially కీ (kī). Lock: తాళం.
Attached to the noun: గదిలో, ఇంట్లో.

phrases.en: This is our home, come in.
Where did you put the key? (informal)
Our flat is on the second floor.

grammar.title: Where things are: -లో, మీద, కింద ...
grammar.body:
Location words come **after** the noun. **-లో** (-lō, in) is a suffix written joined to the noun; the others are separate postpositions: **మీద** (on), **కింద** (under), **దగ్గర** (near, at), **పక్కన** (beside), **ముందు** (in front of), **వెనక** (behind), **లోపల** (inside), **బయట** (outside).

Before these, some nouns use an **oblique stem**: ఇల్లు → ఇంటి (ఇంట్లో, ఇంటి ముందు); ఊరు → ఊరి (ఊళ్ళో). Nouns in -ం keep the m: పుస్తకంలో, పుస్తకం మీద. Pronouns use their possessive form: *నా దగ్గర* (with me), *మీ పక్కన* (next to you).

The verb is the 'being somewhere' verb ఉండు: *ఉంది* (one thing/woman), *ఉన్నాయి* (things), *ఉన్నాడు/ఉన్నారు* (people).

examples.en: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the bed.
The car is outside the house.
The bag is behind the door.
The pharmacy is next to the bank.

grammar.title: There is / there are
grammar.body:
'There is' is simply the verb **ఉండు** after the place: *ఇంట్లో మూడు గదులు ఉన్నాయి* (in the house three rooms are). Use **ఉంది** for one thing, **ఉన్నాయి** for several things, **ఉన్నాడు / ఉన్నారు** for people.

The negative is **లేదు** (one thing), **లేవు** (things), **లేడు** (a man), **లేరు** (people). Add -ā for a question: *ఉందా?*, *ఉన్నాయా?*

To say you **have** an object with you, use **దగ్గర**: *నా దగ్గర పెన్ను ఉంది* (I have a pen [on me]). The dative నాకు is for relatives, illnesses and abstract things.

examples.en: There are three rooms in the house.
There is no fan in the room.
There are no books on the table.

dialogue.title: Where are my keys?
dialogue.setting: Ravi is late for college and can't find his keys. His mother helps.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.en: It's not in the bag either.

lines.speaker: Amma
lines.en: Did you look under the bed?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.en: Ah! Here it is, under the bed!

culture: Shoes and sandals are taken off at the door of a Telugu home, and always before entering the kitchen or the *pūja* (prayer) room. Many homes have a small shrine, and the front threshold is decorated each morning with a *muggu* (rangoli) pattern drawn in rice flour. In apartments, the *watchman* and the building's *association* are central to daily life.
